standard_prerequisites.name: Surjective map
standard_prerequisites.statement: f is surjective when trunc(-1)(fiber_f b) holds for every b.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is one of the two hypotheses of the converse direction and the conclusion of the forward direction.

standard_prerequisites.name: Embedding
standard_prerequisites.statement: f is an embedding when ap f : (x = y) -> (f x = f y) is an equivalence for all x, y.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is used to produce r : x = y with ap f (r) = p `ct` opp q.

standard_prerequisites.name: Paths in a sigma type
standard_prerequisites.statement: (x,p) = (y,q) in a sigma type is equivalent to a pair (r, trans r p = q).
standard_prerequisites.use: It rearranges the equality at source line 584 into the transport statement.

core_obligations: Forward direction: if f is an equivalence then each fiber is contractible, hence its truncation is inhabited, so f is surjective; and the retained result shows every equivalence is an embedding (source lines 575-576).
Converse: assume f is a surjective embedding and fix b : B, aiming to show that the fiber of f at b is contractible (source lines 578-579).
Surjectivity provides a merely existing a : A with f(a) = b, so the fiber is inhabited; it remains to show it is a mere proposition (source lines 580-581).
Given x, y with p : f(x) = b and q : f(y) = b, use that ap f is an equivalence to find r : x = y with ap f (r) = p `ct` opp q (source lines 582-583).

Rearrange that equality by the characterisation of paths in sigma types into trans r p = q, so that r together with it exhibits (x,p) = (y,q) in the fiber, proving the fiber a mere proposition (source lines 584-585).

proof_roadmap.step: Forward direction: contractible fibers and the retained embedding result.
Converse: reduce to the fiber being a mere proposition.
Build the comparison path in the fiber from the embedding property.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 4.6.3 at source lines 571-573: f is an equivalence if and only if it is surjective and an embedding. The author's proof (source lines 574-586) separates the two directions cleanly and the converse is a real argument: surjectivity gives only a truncated inhabitant of the fiber, so after that step the work is to show the fiber is a mere proposition (lines 578-581), and for two fiber elements (x,p) and (y,q) the embedding property produces r : x = y with ap f (r) = p `ct` opp q (lines 582-583), which must then be rearranged by the characterisation of paths in sigma types into the transport statement trans r p = q before r and it can be exhibited as a path in the fiber (lines 584-585). The statement gives no hint that the embedding property is used to produce a path in the source that is then transported.
